deadline.value: The priority deadline for fall admission is January 10, 2027; late applications are accepted through May 7.
deadline.quote: January 10 – Fall Semester General Admissions Deadline: Priority financial assistance (Ph.D. Program Teaching Assistantships are awarded).

fee_waiver.value: A limited number of fee waivers exist, but eligibility is restricted to U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents.
fee_waiver.quote: Domestic applicant (citizen or lawful permanent resident of the United States)

also.quote: A limited number of application fee waivers are available for qualified Ph.D. applicants.

gre_general.value: The GRE is optional; you may send General or Subject scores to the Graduate College.
gre_general.quote: OPTIONAL: Submit official Graduate Record Exam (GRE) scores (General and/or Subject specific test) directly to the Graduate College.

gre_subject.value: A subject-specific GRE is optional, not required.
gre_subject.quote: OPTIONAL: Submit official Graduate Record Exam (GRE) scores (General and/or Subject specific test) directly to the Graduate College.

supervisor.value: Students are admitted by the program and declare a major advisor only after three rotations in the first semester.
supervisor.quote: All students accepted into the program on teaching assistantships will complete three 5-week long rotations during their first semester before declaring their Major Advisor.

funding.value: Teaching assistantships with a $25,000 stipend are offered on a competitive basis each fall.
funding.quote: These assistantships are offered on a competitive basis every Fall semester

also.quote: All Ph.D. applicants are automatically considered for program funded Teaching Assistantships (TAs), which come with a tuition and fee waiver, student health insurance, and an annual stipend of $25,000.

entry_route.value: A bachelor's or graduate degree in an appropriate scientific discipline, with a GPA of at least 3.00, is required.
entry_route.quote: An applicant must hold a baccalaureate or graduate degree in an appropriate scientific discipline with a minimum GPA of 3.00.

notes: Interdisciplinary program. The core sequence is taught by Biological Sciences, Chemistry and Biochemistry, and Physics faculty. Fee waivers are requested by emailing the program with the required materials.
name: Biomolecular Sciences PhD
